about
Built entirely from scratch in Cinema 4D and Octane, this project reimagines the NODE ecosystem within a carefully constructed domestic environment. I modeled the products and surrounding elements myself, developing the space around the relationship between technology, furniture, light, and everyday objects. Rather than presenting each product in isolation, the scenes treat the ecosystem as a connected system, using warm lighting, muted materials, and considered compositions to create a cohesive visual language. The result is a speculative product film that combines product visualization with environmental storytelling, using CGI to give the NODE ecosystem a distinct physical and atmospheric identity.

Jan 2025
about
For this project, I modeled and animated the KO II entirely in Cinema 4D and Octane, breaking the sampler down into its individual components and reconstructing it through an exploded-view animation. The project focuses on the distinct visual language of the device—from its grid of tactile controls and graphic interface elements to its layered construction and playful industrial details. By separating each component and giving it space to move independently, the animation turns the product’s internal structure into the main visual narrative while retaining the simplicity and character of Teenage Engineering’s design language.

about
Not Your Average Tee is a collection I designed, developed, and released as an exploration of how my visual language could exist beyond the screen. The project brings together graphic design, typography, imagery, and apparel into a series of pieces built around a distinct attitude rather than a single visual formula. From developing the graphics to figuring out how they translate onto physical garments, the collection became an exercise in building something tangible from ideas that usually live within my design practice.

about
This project began as an R&D study while learning and experimenting with cloth simulation in 3D. Rather than working toward a specific commercial outcome, I used the process to understand how different forces, collisions, folds, and fabric properties could be controlled to create interesting forms. The final visuals came out of that experimentation, turning what started as a technical study into a collection of atmospheric compositions worth presenting on their own.

about
Sound Studies is an ongoing collection of personal poster work created around artists, albums, and tracks that have influenced my listening. Each piece is an opportunity to interpret sound through typography, image-making, composition, and visual systems rather than simply reproduce an existing identity. The collection allows me to experiment freely with different aesthetics and approaches while exploring how the energy, mood, and character of music can be translated into a static visual language.

about
Frequency Fields is an exploration of audio-reactive systems built in TouchDesigner, where incoming sound is translated into movement, density, scale, and spatial behaviour in real time. The project focuses on the relationship between audio and procedural visuals, using particles as a medium to make sound physically visible. Rather than animating the visuals to a fixed track, the system responds dynamically to changes in the audio, creating a generative visual that continuously evolves with the music.

about
This project is a speculative product film for Solana Seeker, built around the idea of making an inherently digital ecosystem feel physical. The visual direction explores Seeker beyond its role as a smartphone, focusing on its connection to digital assets, decentralized applications, identity, and the broader Solana ecosystem. Through 3D product visualization, controlled environments, and cinematic movement, the film creates a visual language around the relationship between hardware and the onchain world. The result is a conceptual interpretation of Seeker designed to make an otherwise abstract digital ecosystem feel tangible and immediate.

about
Created entirely from scratch in Cinema 4D and Octane, this project is a focused product visualization of the Solflare Card. I modeled the card, built the environment, developed the materials, and designed the lighting and composition to create a polished, tactile representation of the product. The aim was to translate a digital-first Web3 product into a physical object with weight, texture, and presence, using controlled reflections, surface details, and studio-style lighting to highlight the card’s form and finish.
